segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For I do not want you to be unaware, brothers and sisters, that our ancestors were all under the cloud and all passed through the sea,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and all were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and all ate the same spiritual food,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and all drank the same spiritual drink; for they drank from a spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But God was not pleased with most of them, for they were laid low in the wilderness.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now these things happened as examples for us, so that we would not be people who crave evil, as they also craved.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Do not become idolaters, as some of them were; as it is written:

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to revel.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Let us not commit sexual immorality, as some of them did, and twenty-three thousand fell in a single day.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Let us not put Christ to the test, as some of them tested him, and were destroyed by the snakes.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And do not grumble, as some of them grumbled, and were destroyed by the destroyer.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now these things were happening to them as examples, and they were written down to warn us, on whom the ends of the ages have come.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So anyone who thinks they are standing should watch out that they do not fall.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: No testing has overtaken you that is not common to humanity. And God is faithful: he will not let you be tested beyond what you are able, but with the testing he will also provide the way out, so that you are able to endure it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Therefore, my dear friends, flee from idolatry.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: I speak as to sensible people; judge for yourselves what I say.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The cup of blessing that we bless, is it not a sharing in the blood of Christ? The bread that we break, is it not a sharing in the body of Christ?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Because there is one bread, we who are many are one body, for we all partake of the one bread.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Look at Israel according to the flesh: are not those who eat the sacrifices sharers in the altar?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: What then am I saying? That food sacrificed to an idol is anything, or that an idol is anything?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: No, but that what they sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to God, and I do not want you to become sharers with demons.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons; you cannot partake of the table of the Lord and the table of demons.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Or are we provoking the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than he is?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: “Everything is permitted”—but not everything is beneficial. “Everything is permitted”—but not everything builds up.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Let no one seek their own good, but the good of the other person.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Eat everything sold in the meat market without raising any question on account of conscience,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “the earth is the Lord’s, and all that fills it.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: If one of the unbelievers invites you and you want to go, eat everything set before you without raising any question on account of conscience.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But if someone says to you,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “This was offered in sacrifice,”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: do not eat it, on account of the one who told you and on account of conscience.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: By conscience I mean not your own but the other person’s. For why should my freedom be judged by another’s conscience?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: If I partake with thanks, why am I slandered over what I give thanks for?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So whether you eat or drink or whatever you do, do everything for the glory of God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Give no cause for stumbling to Jews or to Greeks or to the assembly of God,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: just as I also try to please everyone in everything, not seeking my own benefit but that of the many, so that they may be saved.

notes.phrase: a spiritual rock that followed them
notes.note: Israel is given water from a rock near the start of the wilderness journey (Exodus 17) and again near its end (Numbers 20). Jewish interpreters of the period spoke of a well or rock that traveled with the people, and Paul appears to draw on that tradition, identifying the source of the water with Christ.

The Greek word means a pattern, model or mold. Some interpreters take it more strongly here as “types”, meaning events designed to prefigure the situation of Paul’s readers. Others take it simply as warning examples. The related adverb in verse 11 is rendered the same way.

The quotation is Exodus 32:6, from the golden calf episode. The verb covers playing, dancing and festive merrymaking; “play” is the traditional rendering, but in modern English it suggests children’s games, where the scene is one of celebration around an idol.

The reference is to the episode at Baal of Peor in Numbers 25, where the Hebrew and Greek texts both give twenty-four thousand. The reason for Paul’s figure is not known; proposed explanations include a slip of memory, a round number, or a different tradition, and none is certain.

Some important early manuscripts read “the Lord” here, and a few read “God”. “Christ” is the reading of the edition translated and is widely thought more likely to be original, since copyists would have found it harder to speak of Israel in the wilderness testing Christ.

Most English versions have “temptation” and “tempted” in this verse. The Greek noun and its verb mean a putting to the proof, and in the Greek Old Testament they are the usual words for Israel’s trials in the wilderness, which Paul has just recalled. Scholars disagree whether trial or enticement to sin is in view here; the two overlap, since the testing in question is pressure to join in idolatry.

The older tradition has “communion”, and many modern versions have “participation” or “sharing”. The Greek word means having something in common, here taking part in a thing together. The related noun in verses 18 and 20 is rendered “sharers” so that the link in Paul’s argument stays visible.

notes.traditional: the things which the Gentiles sacrifice
notes.note: Many manuscripts name the subject, “the Gentiles”; the edition translated omits it as a probable clarifying addition. The sense is the same either way: “they” are the pagan worshipers, not Israel of verse 18. The wording echoes Deuteronomy 32:17.

Most scholars think Paul is quoting a slogan current at Corinth, which he then qualifies, and the quotation marks reflect that view. Greek manuscripts have no quotation marks, so the words can also be read as Paul’s own statement. The same saying appears at 6:12.

notes.traditional: This is offered in sacrifice unto idols
notes.note: The speaker uses the ordinary, respectful Greek term for meat from a temple sacrifice, not the disparaging “sacrificed to an idol” of verse 19; this is how a pagan, or someone speaking in a pagan’s house, would put it. Later manuscripts replace it with the “idol” word and repeat the quotation from verse 26 at the end of the verse.

The Greek word can mean grace or thanks. Older versions read “by grace”, but most modern translators take it as thankfulness, because it is picked up at once by the related verb “give thanks”, referring to the prayer said over a meal.

“Church” is the near-universal rendering, and readers know what it refers to. The Greek word was the ordinary term for a civic gathering and the Greek Old Testament’s word for Israel assembled before God. “Assembly” is used throughout this translation because “church” now suggests a building or an institution.

candidates.reason: The plural vocative addressing a mixed congregation recurs in every letter, and versions split between “brothers” and “brothers and sisters”.
The plural for Israel’s forebears recurs across Acts, Paul and Hebrews, and “fathers”, “ancestors” and “forefathers” are all in use.
As an address it recurs throughout the letters, and “beloved” versus “dear friends” should be fixed, especially given its use of Jesus as “beloved Son”.
The verb and its cognates recur widely, and translators vary among “fornication”, “sexual immorality” and “prostitution”.
It recurs in Acts 15, 1 Corinthians 8–10 and Revelation 2, with varying renderings (“meat”, “food”, “things” offered or sacrificed to idols).
